activities.title: Count the coins
activities.intro: These are coins. Count how many you see, then tap the number.
activities.offScreen: Go find three coins in a jar or a wallet and count them with a grown-up.

rounds.prompt: A coin sits next to a cup. How many coins do you see? Count them and tap the number.
Look at the coins on the table. How many coins do you see? Count them and tap the number.
Look at the coins on the table. How many coins do you see? Count them and tap the number.
Here is a stack of coins next to a cup. How many coins are in the stack? Count them and tap the number.

activities.title: Match the number
activities.intro: Each pile has some coins. Listen for the number, then tap the pile that has that many.
activities.offScreen: Go ask a grown-up for three coins and put them in a pile.

rounds.prompt: Listen for the number. Tap the pile that has three.
Listen for the number. Tap the pile that has one.
Listen for the number. Tap the pile that has two.
Listen for the number. Tap the pile that has three.

activities.title: More or fewer coins
activities.intro: Look at the two piles of coins. Tap the pile the question asks for.
activities.offScreen: Go find two piles of coins, one bigger and one smaller, and show a grown-up which pile has more.

rounds.prompt: Tap the pile with more coins.
Tap the pile with more coins.
Tap the pile with fewer coins.
Tap the pile with more coins.

parentCard.title: Real coins, real counting
steps: Real coins are the best counters for this activity. Keep them within your sight when they handle them: small coins are a choking hazard at this age.
Find a counting book with pictures they can point to and read it together.
Pause on each page and count the pictures out loud together.
Tip a few real coins out of a jar and count them together, one at a time.
Make a small pile and a bigger pile and ask them which pile has more.
notice: Do they touch each coin once as they count, or do they skip or double-count?
Do they know that the last number they say is the total, not just a word in a list?
